# The seven sweeps

Run in order. After each sweep, loop back over the earlier sweeps to make sure the new edits did not break them.

## 1. Clarity

Check for confusing sentence structures, unclear pronouns, jargon, ambiguous statements and missing context. Mark problem areas first, then propose edits that keep the original intent. Confirm each section has one main idea and speaks to the reader ("you").

## 2. Voice and tone

Read aloud. Look for shifts between formal and casual, mixed "we" and "the company", humor that appears and disappears, and words that do not fit the brand. Smooth the transitions so one personality runs throughout.

## 3. So what

For every statement ask "so what?". Features need a benefit bridge ("which means..."). Example: "Uses AI analytics" becomes "Spots trends you would miss, so you decide faster." Company achievements that do not help the reader get cut or reframed.

## 4. Prove it

List every claim that needs proof and check whether proof is nearby: named testimonials, case studies, statistics, third-party validation, guarantees, review scores. Flag "trusted by thousands", "industry-leading", "customers love us" without evidence. Recommend adding proof or softening the claim.

## 5. Specificity

Replace vague words ("improve", "optimize", "enhance") with numbers, timeframes or concrete examples, but only with facts the user can confirm. Content that cannot be made specific is often filler and can be cut.

| Vague | Specific (only if true) |
| --- | --- |
| Save time | Save 4 hours every week |
| Many customers | 2,847 teams |
| Fast results | Results in 14 days |
| Great support | Replies within 2 hours |

## 6. Emotion

Does the copy make the reader feel the current pain and the better outcome? Use a vivid "before" state, sensory language or a short true story. Emotion must serve the message and stay honest; never manipulate with false urgency or fear.

## 7. Zero risk

Focus on the area around each CTA. List every reason someone might hesitate and check the copy answers it: guarantees, free trial terms, "cancel anytime" (only if true), privacy assurances, what happens after clicking, social proof near the CTA. Replace a vague "Contact us" with a clear next step.

## Quick checks

- Cut: very, really, extremely, just, actually, basically, in order to, things, stuff.
- Replace: utilize with use, leverage with use, facilitate with help, implement with set up.
- Watch: adverbs, passive voice, nominalizations ("make a decision" becomes "decide").
- Sentences: one idea each, varied length, important information first, usually under 25 words.
- Paragraphs: one topic, 2-4 sentences on the web, strong first sentence.

## Optional expert panel (high-stakes copy)

For launch pages, pricing pages and launch emails, review the copy from 3-5 viewpoints (for example conversion copywriter, target customer, brand strategist, skeptical buyer). Score each 1-10 with specific critiques and address the lowest scores first. Present scores as opinions, not measurements.

## Content refresh

When editing older content: update outdated statistics and examples (with sources), check that product details are current, re-check the brand voice and confirm links still work.
